title.en: Email and streaming media

description.en: Understand why a message passes through two servers, and why the envelope and the header carry two sets of addresses; and understand how a video plays while it downloads thanks to buffering, error correction and compression, and why live streams and calls each work differently.
description.zh: 懂得一封信为什么要经过两台服务器、信封与首部为什么是两套地址；也懂得一段视频怎样靠缓冲、纠错和压缩边下边播，以及直播和通话为什么各有各的做法。

name.en: Email architecture: user agent and message transfer agent (MTA)
name.zh: 电子邮件的架构：用户代理与邮件传输代理 (email architecture, user agent, MTA)
邮件格式与 MIME (message format, MIME)

name.en: Final delivery: POP3, IMAP and webmail
name.zh: 最终投递：POP3、IMAP 与网页邮件 (POP3, IMAP, webmail)

name.en: Kinds of streaming media, their requirements and playback models (RTSP, RTP)
name.zh: 流媒体的种类、要求与播放模型 (streaming media, RTSP, RTP)

name.en: Jitter and the client-side playout buffer
name.zh: 抖动与客户端缓冲 (jitter, playout buffer)

name.en: Handling packet loss: forward error correction and error concealment
name.zh: 丢包处理：前向纠错与差错掩盖 (forward error correction, error concealment)
多媒体压缩：无损与有损 (compression, lossless vs lossy)
直播与实时会议 (live streaming, real-time conferencing, SIP)

description.en: Thinking email goes straight from the sender's computer to the recipient's computer. In fact there are two always-on mail servers in between: the sender can leave as soon as the message is handed over, and the recipient's computer being off does not lose the message.
description.zh: 以为邮件是发件人的电脑直接连到收件人的电脑。实际上中间有两台常年在线的邮件服务器：发信人交出去就能走，收信人关机也不丢信。

description.en: Thinking the whole path is SMTP. SMTP only pushes the message out (submission and the transfer between servers); Bob fetches his mail with POP3 or IMAP.
description.zh: 以为整条路都是 SMTP。SMTP 只管把信推出去（提交和服务器之间的传输），Bob 取信用的是 POP3 或 IMAP。

description.en: Thinking the Bcc recipient is written in the header for everyone to see, or that SMTP decides who to deliver to by reading the header. In fact delivery follows the envelope, and Bcc recipients appear only in the envelope.
description.zh: 以为 Bcc 的收件人会写在首部里让大家看到，或者以为 SMTP 靠首部决定把信送给谁。实际上送信看信封，Bcc 的人只出现在信封里。

description.en: Thinking that with webmail the whole path is HTTP. HTTP exists only between the browser and the web front end; between servers it is still SMTP.
description.zh: 以为用了网页邮件，整条路都是 HTTP。HTTP 只在浏览器和网页前端之间，服务器与服务器之间仍是 SMTP。

description.en: Thinking a bigger buffer is always better. A big buffer resists jitter, but you wait longer before playback starts, which is fatal for a video call.
description.zh: 以为缓冲越大越好。缓冲大虽然抗抖动，但开播前要等更久，对视频通话更是致命。

description.en: Thinking lost packets in a call should also be retransmitted. A retransmitted packet arrives long after its playback moment and also slows the packets behind it; in a call, a late packet is as good as lost.
description.zh: 以为通话里的丢包也该重传。重传来的包早已过了播放时刻，还会拖慢后面的包；通话里晚到的包等于丢了。

description.en: Thinking lossy compression just means “poor quality”. Lossy compression throws away what people cannot perceive, in exchange for a very large compression ratio.
description.zh: 以为有损压缩就是“质量差”。有损压缩丢掉的是人感觉不到的部分，换来很大的压缩比。

description.en: Thinking one parity packet can recover any number of lost packets. One parity packet can repair only one lost packet in its group.
description.zh: 以为一个校验包能救回任意多个丢包。一个校验包只能修复其所在那一组里的一个丢包。

title.en: Why not deliver it directly?

prompt.en: In your dorm you have written a message to Bob. The most direct way: your computer connects straight to Bob's computer and puts the message in his hands. What is the biggest problem with this?
prompt.zh: 你在宿舍写好一封信给 Bob。最直接的办法：你的电脑直接连上 Bob 的电脑，把信交到他手里。这个办法最大的毛病是什么？

label.en: Bob's computer may be off or offline, so the message has nowhere to go
label.zh: Bob 的电脑可能没开机、不在线，信就没处放

feedback.en: Right. A message needs somewhere that is always online and can receive it on his behalf first.
feedback.zh: 对。信需要一个常年在线、能先代收的地方。

label.en: A message is too long for a TCP connection to carry
label.zh: 一封信太长，TCP 连接传不了

feedback.en: TCP can carry a byte stream of any length, so length is not the issue.
feedback.zh: TCP 能传任意长的字节流，长度不是问题。

label.en: You cannot find out Bob's IP address
label.zh: 你没法知道 Bob 的 IP 地址

feedback.en: The address can be looked up with DNS (Lesson 14). The real trouble is whether he is there right now.
feedback.zh: 地址可以用 DNS 问出来（第 14 课）。真正的麻烦是对方此刻在不在。

explain.en: People do not keep their computers on all the time waiting for mail, and the sender will not sit at the computer waiting for the other side to come online. So email works like posting a physical letter: first hand it to an always-staffed “post office”, which then finds a way to deliver it.
explain.zh: 人不会一直开着电脑等信，发信的人也不会守在电脑前等对方上线。所以邮件的做法和寄实体信一样：先交给一个常年值班的“邮局”，再由邮局想办法送到。

title.en: Two kinds of roles, a journey in three steps

text.en: There are only two kinds of roles in an email system. The **user agent** is the program in your hands, such as Outlook, and it writes messages, reads them and sorts them into folders. The **message transfer agent** (MTA) is the mail server, such as Exchange, and it moves messages from the sender's side to the recipient's side.
text.zh: 邮件系统里只有两类角色。**用户代理** (user agent) 是你手里的程序，比如 Outlook，负责写信、读信、分文件夹。**邮件传输代理** (message transfer agent, MTA) 就是邮件服务器，比如 Exchange，负责把信从发信方搬到收信方。

alt.en: Alice's user agent reaches Bob's user agent through two mail servers in three steps, submission, transfer and final delivery, using SMTP, SMTP, and POP3 or IMAP in turn
alt.zh: Alice 的用户代理经提交、传输、最终投递三步，穿过两台邮件服务器到达 Bob 的用户代理，协议依次是 SMTP、SMTP、POP3 或 IMAP

caption.en: The three steps of a message: submission, transfer, final delivery
caption.zh: 一封信的三步：提交、传输、最终投递

text.en: The three steps are: **mail submission**, where Alice's user agent hands the message to her own server; **message transfer**, where the two servers pass the message across; and **final delivery**, where Bob's user agent fetches the message from his server.
text.zh: 三步分别是：**邮件提交** (mail submission)，Alice 的用户代理把信交给自己的服务器；**邮件传输** (message transfer)，两台服务器之间把信送过去；**最终投递** (final delivery)，Bob 的用户代理从他的服务器上取信。

title.en: Why two servers, and why only the first two steps are SMTP
title.zh: 为什么要两台服务器，为什么只有前两步是 SMTP

text.en: The opening question has two halves of an answer, each landing on one server.
text.zh: 开头的问题有两半答案，各落在一台服务器身上。

text.en: **The receiving half.** Bob's computer may be off. Bob's server is always online and first takes the message into his **mailbox**; whenever Bob turns his computer on, that is when he comes to collect it.
text.zh: **收信这一半。** Bob 的电脑可能没开机。Bob 的服务器常年在线，先把信收进他的**邮箱** (mailbox)，Bob 什么时候开机，什么时候来取。

text.en: **The sending half.** Alice clicks send and may immediately close her laptop and drop off Wi-Fi. If her computer had to stand guard in person until the message had really arrived at Bob's side, losing the connection would undo everything; and if Bob's side were busy or unreachable for a moment, she would have to retry again and again. So she only has to hand the message to her own server and can leave: that server is always online, and if it cannot reach Bob's server, it puts the message in a queue and tries again after a while.
text.zh: **发信这一半。** Alice 点了发送，可能立刻合上笔记本、断开 Wi-Fi。要是她的电脑得亲自守着，直到信真的送进 Bob 那边，一断线就前功尽弃；Bob 那边偶尔忙或连不上，她还得一遍遍重试。所以她只要把信交给自己的服务器就可以走人：这台服务器常年在线，连不上 Bob 的服务器，就把信放进队列，隔一阵再试。

text.en: One server guards the delivery for the sender, and one guards the receipt for the recipient. That is the reason for two servers.
text.zh: 一台替发信人守着送，一台替收信人守着收，这就是两台服务器的理由。

text.en: The first two steps use the same protocol, SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol), saying the same thing in different settings: submission means “I entrust this message to you”, and transfer means “on behalf of my user, I am handing this message to you”. Who connects to whom, and on which port, also differs:
text.zh: 前两步用的是同一个协议 SMTP（简单邮件传输协议，Simple Mail Transfer Protocol），说同一种话，场合不同：提交是“我把信托付给你”，传输是“我替我的用户，把这封信递给你”。连谁、走哪个端口也不同：

rows.zh: Alice 的用户代理 → Alice 的服务器
Alice 的服务器 → Bob 的服务器

rows.en: Bob's user agent fetches from Bob's server
rows.zh: Bob 的用户代理 向 Bob 的服务器取信

text.en: Why does the last step no longer use SMTP? Because SMTP is “push”: the sending side connects, and the other side has to be online right then to receive. Bob's computer may not be online, so the last step becomes “pull”: when Bob wants to read, he goes to the server and fetches the mail himself.
text.zh: 为什么最后一步不再用 SMTP？因为 SMTP 是“推”：发的一方连上去，对方得此刻在线接收。Bob 的电脑未必在线，所以最后一步改成“拉”：Bob 想看时，自己去服务器上取。

title.en: Do not mix them up

body.en: SMTP appears twice, but the whole journey of a message is not SMTP: the receiving step uses POP3 or IMAP.
body.zh: SMTP 出现两次，但邮件的全程不是 SMTP：收信这一步用 POP3 或 IMAP。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: how Alice's server finds Bob's server
summary.zh: 超出课件：Alice 的服务器怎么找到 Bob 的服务器

text.en: It uses DNS to look up the mail server record for the recipient's domain (the part after the @), called an MX record (the DNS from Lesson 14 is used once more here).
text.zh: 它用 DNS 查收件人域名（@ 后面那部分）的邮件服务器记录，叫 MX 记录（第 14 课讲过的 DNS 在这里再用一次）。

title.en: Where is the message now?

prompt.en: Alice clicks send and immediately closes her laptop to go to class. Bob's computer is also off at that moment. A few minutes later, where is the message?
prompt.zh: Alice 点了发送，马上合上笔记本去上课。Bob 的电脑那时也关着。几分钟后，这封信在哪里？

label.en: In the mailbox on Bob's mail server; once Bob turns on his computer, his user agent fetches it itself
label.zh: 在 Bob 的邮件服务器的邮箱里；等 Bob 开机后，他的用户代理自己去取

feedback.en: Right. Submission and transfer are both done by always-online servers, and the last step is Bob pulling it himself.
feedback.zh: 对。提交、传输都由常年在线的服务器完成，最后一步是 Bob 自己来拉。

label.en: Still in Alice's laptop, and it can only be sent once Bob's computer and Alice's are both on
label.zh: 还在 Alice 的笔记本里，要等 Bob 开机、Alice 也开机，才能送出去

feedback.en: The submission step has already handed the message to Alice's server, so the laptop can leave and does not need to stand guard.
feedback.zh: 提交那一步已经把信交给了 Alice 的服务器，笔记本可以走了，不用守着。

label.en: Queued in Alice's server, which will push it to Bob's computer with SMTP once he turns it on
label.zh: 在 Alice 的服务器里排队，等 Bob 开机后，服务器用 SMTP 把信推到他的电脑上

feedback.en: The transfer step's target is Bob's mail server (which is always online), not Bob's computer. Bob's computer fetches the mail itself with POP3 or IMAP.
feedback.zh: 传输那一步的对象是 Bob 的邮件服务器（它一直在线），不是 Bob 的电脑。Bob 的电脑是自己用 POP3 或 IMAP 去取。

label.en: Already in Bob's laptop, he just has not opened it yet
label.zh: 已经在 Bob 的笔记本里了，只是他还没打开

feedback.en: A computer that is off cannot receive mail. The message waits on his server for him to come and fetch it.
feedback.zh: 关着的电脑收不了信。信停在他的服务器上，等他来取。

explain.en: As soon as the message is handed to Alice's server, her computer can leave; the transfer step is server to server, so the message lands in Bob's mailbox, and Bob's computer fetches it later on its own. Two always-online servers absorb the fact that the other side is not online.
explain.zh: 信一交给 Alice 的服务器，她的电脑就可以走了；传输那一步是服务器对服务器，信落进 Bob 的邮箱，Bob 的电脑是后来自己去取的。两台常年在线的服务器，把“对方不在线”这件事吸收掉了。

title.en: Envelope and letter: two sets of addresses

text.en: If you have posted a physical letter, you get it: the postman looks only at the address on the **envelope** and does not open the letter; the “Dear all” written on the letter is for the reader. Email is the same, with two sets of things:
text.zh: 寄过实体信就懂：邮递员只看**信封**上的地址，不拆信；信纸上写的“亲爱的各位”是给读信人看的。邮件也一样，有两套东西：

rows.en: The user agent, for people to read

rows.zh: MAIL FROM（信封发件人）、RCPT TO（收件人）

rows.en: To, Cc, Bcc, From, Subject, etc.

text.en: A message is laid out as the header, a blank line, then the body. An address is written `username@domain`, for example `bob@ee.uwa.edu.au`: before the @ is the mailbox name, and after the @ is a DNS name used to find the server.
text.zh: 一封信由首部、一个空行、正文依次排成。地址的写法是 `用户名@域名`，例如 `bob@ee.uwa.edu.au`：@ 前是邮箱名，@ 后是一个 DNS 名字，用来找到服务器。

text.en: Why two sets? Because “who the letter says it is for” and “who it is actually delivered to” can differ. The classic case is Bcc (blind carbon copy). In Alice's message, To is Bob, Cc is Carol and Bcc is Dave, and what goes out looks like this:
text.zh: 为什么要两套？因为“信纸上写给谁”和“实际送给谁”可以不一样。最典型的是 Bcc（密送，blind carbon copy）。Alice 的信，To 是 Bob，Cc 是 Carol，Bcc 是 Dave，送出去的样子是：

blocks.code:
信封（SMTP 看这个）
MAIL FROM:<alice@student.unimelb.edu.au>
RCPT TO:<bob@ee.uwa.edu.au>
RCPT TO:<carol@example.com>
RCPT TO:<dave@example.org>

首部和正文（人看这个）
From: alice@student.unimelb.edu.au
To: bob@ee.uwa.edu.au
Cc: carol@example.com
Subject: hello

Hi everyone, ...

caption.en: Dave appears only in the envelope

text.en: How do the two sets of addresses line up? The envelope does not come from nowhere: the program that writes the message (the slides say the transfer agent can also do this) reads the To, Cc and Bcc fields, lines everyone in them up as a series of RCPT TO lines, and then removes the Bcc line from the message before handing it over. The server only recognises the envelope, so Dave still receives it; he is not in the header, so Bob and Carol cannot see him.
text.zh: 两套地址怎么对上？信封不是凭空来的：写信的程序（课件说，传输代理也可以做这件事）读出 To、Cc、Bcc 三栏，把里面所有的人排成一串 RCPT TO，再把 Bcc 那一行从信里拿掉，才把信交出去。服务器只认信封，所以 Dave 照样收到；首部里没有他，Bob 和 Carol 就看不到。

title.en: Where is Dave?

prompt.en: Alice sends a message: To is Bob, Cc is Carol, Bcc is Dave. Which statement is correct?
prompt.zh: Alice 发信：To 是 Bob，Cc 是 Carol，Bcc 是 Dave。下面哪种说法正确？

label.en: The envelope has three recipients, Bob, Carol and Dave; the header that Bob and Carol receive does not contain Dave
label.zh: 信封里有 Bob、Carol、Dave 三个收件人；Bob 和 Carol 收到的首部里没有 Dave

feedback.en: Right. Delivery relies on the envelope, and secrecy comes from not writing him in the header.
feedback.zh: 对。送信靠信封，保密靠首部不写。

label.en: Dave is written only in the Bcc line of the header and does not need to be in the envelope
label.zh: Dave 只写在首部的 Bcc 里，信封里不用有

feedback.en: SMTP does not read the header, only the envelope. If Dave is not in the envelope, nobody delivers the message to him.
feedback.zh: SMTP 不看首部，只看信封。信封里没有 Dave，就没人把信送给他。

label.en: The header still says Bcc: Dave, and the user agent just hides it without displaying it
label.zh: 首部里照样写着 Bcc: Dave，只是用户代理把它藏起来不显示

feedback.en: Then Carol's copy would carry Dave's address, and you would be relying on her program not to display it, so secrecy would be unreliable.
feedback.zh: 那样 Carol 的信里就带着 Dave 的地址，还得指望她的程序不显示，保密就靠不住了。

explain.en: This is exactly the point of two sets of addresses: the envelope decides who it is delivered to, and the header decides what others see. A Bcc recipient appears only in the envelope.
explain.zh: 两套地址的意义就在这里：信封决定送给谁，首部决定别人看到什么。Bcc 的收件人只在信封里。

title.en: From, Sender, Return-Path, Received

text.en: For the header lines that are easy to confuse, remember them as “who wrote it, who sent it, where it bounces back, who stamped it on the way”:
text.zh: 首部里容易混的几行，用“谁写的、谁寄的、往哪退、路上谁盖过章”来记：

rows.en: The secretary who sends it for the boss
The route a bounce takes when something goes wrong, pointing back to the envelope sender (MAIL FROM)
rows.zh: 出问题时退信走的路，指回信封发件人 (MAIL FROM)

rows.en: Each server that handles the message adds a line at the top, like a postmark
rows.zh: 每台经手的服务器在最上面加一行，像邮戳

rows.en: One line added per server passed
rows.zh: 每过一台服务器加一行

text.en: From and Sender can be two different people, just as the boss signs and the secretary sends. A bounce goes back to the sender in the envelope and ignores From.
text.zh: From 和 Sender 可以是两个人，就像领导署名、秘书发出。退信则是回到信封里的发件人，不看 From。

text.en: Received accumulates along the way: each server adds its own line at the very top, so the newest is at the top, and **reading from the bottom up** gives the route the message took. When a message comes from an unknown origin or is slow to arrive, these lines tell you at which stop it got stuck.
text.zh: Received 是一路累加的：每台服务器把自己那一行加在最上面，所以最新的在最上面，**从下往上读**，就是这封信走过的路线。信件来路不明、或者迟迟不到时，看这几行就能知道卡在了哪一站。

blocks.code:
Received: from mail.unimelb.edu.au by mail.ee.uwa.edu.au; 10:02:07
Received: from alice-pc by mail.unimelb.edu.au; 10:02:05
From: Alice <alice@student.unimelb.edu.au>
...

caption.en: Illustration: the upper line was added last by Bob's server, the lower line first by Alice's server
caption.zh: 示意：上面一行是 Bob 的服务器最后加的，下面一行是 Alice 的服务器先加的

title.en: How a binary attachment gets through SMTP
title.zh: 二进制附件怎么过 SMTP

intro.en: The SMTP channel carries only ASCII text, while a picture is arbitrary bytes that can have any value; stuffing them in directly would have them treated as control characters, or not fit at all. The remedy: cut every 3 bytes (24 bits) afresh into 4 pieces of 6 bits each, treat each piece as a number from 0 to 63, and write it with one of 64 printable characters. This is called base64: 0 to 25 are A to Z, 26 to 51 are a to z, 52 to 61 are 0 to 9, 62 is +, and 63 is /. Let us encode the three bytes of the text Man.
intro.zh: SMTP 的通道只传 ASCII 文本，而图片是任意字节，什么值都有，直接塞进去会被当成控制字符，或者根本装不下。办法：把每 3 个字节（24 位）重新切成 4 份、每份 6 位，每份当成一个 0 到 63 的数，用 64 个可打印字符表示。这叫 base64：0 到 25 是 A 到 Z，26 到 51 是 a 到 z，52 到 61 是 0 到 9，62 是 +，63 是 /。我们来编码文字 Man 的三个字节。

why.en: The ASCII values of the three characters, exactly three bytes
why.zh: 三个字符的 ASCII 值，正好三个字节

why.en: Ignore the original byte boundaries and regroup every 6 bits, making 4 groups
why.zh: 不管原来的字节边界，每 6 位重新分一组，共 4 组

why.en: Each 6-bit group is a number between 0 and 63
why.zh: 每组 6 位是 0 到 63 之间的数

why.en: Look up the table: 19 is T, 22 is W, 5 is F, 46 is u
why.zh: 查表：19 是 T，22 是 W，5 是 F，46 是 u

outro.en: 3 bytes become 4 characters, so the size becomes 4/3 of the original, about one third more. This is the price paid for being able to travel through an ASCII channel. The receiver reverses it, restoring every 4 characters to 3 bytes.
outro.zh: 3 个字节变成 4 个字符，体积变成原来的 4/3，大约多出三分之一。这是为了能走 ASCII 通道付的代价。收信方反过来，每 4 个字符还原成 3 个字节。

title.en: MIME: giving the body a structure

text.en: The early email format RFC 822 recognised only English ASCII. Later people wanted to send French with accents, Cyrillic, Chinese, and also pictures and sound. The solution is MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions): it gives the body a structure and specifies how non-ASCII is encoded. It adds five headers:
text.zh: 早期的邮件格式 RFC 822 只认英文 ASCII。后来人们要发带重音的法语、西里尔字母、中文，还要发图片和声音。解决办法是 MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions)：给正文加结构，并规定非 ASCII 怎么编码。它新增了五个首部：

rows.en: A description of the content for people to read
A unique identifier for this part
How the body is wrapped so it can be transferred, such as 7bit or base64
rows.zh: 正文怎么包装才能传，比如 7bit 或 base64

text.en: Content-Type is written type/subtype: before the slash is the broad category (text, image, audio, video, model, application, message, multipart), and after the slash is the specific format, for example text/plain, text/html, image/png, audio/mpeg, application/pdf. The receiver uses it to know whom to hand this run of bytes to for interpretation.
text.zh: Content-Type 的写法是 类型/子类型：斜线前是大类（text、image、audio、video、model、application、message、multipart），斜线后是具体格式，例如 text/plain、text/html、image/png、audio/mpeg、application/pdf。收信方靠它知道这一段字节该交给谁去解读。

text.en: A message with attachments uses multipart: the body is divided into several parts, with parts separated by a delimiter line. The delimiter is called the boundary; the writing program picks a string of characters that will not collide with the content and declares it in Content-Type; each part is preceded by two hyphens plus that string, and the last part is closed with two more hyphens at the end. Below, the first part is plain text and the second is a base64-encoded PNG image.
text.zh: 一封信带附件时用 multipart：正文里分成几段，段与段之间用一行分隔符隔开。分隔符叫 boundary，由写信的程序自己挑一串不会和内容撞上的字符，在 Content-Type 里声明；每段前面写两个短横线加这串字符，最后一段收尾时再多加两个短横线。下面第一段是纯文字，第二段是 base64 编码的 PNG 图片。

blocks.code:
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=UniqueBoundary

--UniqueBoundary
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit

This message has an attachment.

--UniqueBoundary
Content-Type: image/png
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64

iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAA... (略)

--UniqueBoundary--

caption.en: multipart/mixed: two independent pieces of content

text.en: There are several kinds of multipart; the difference is in how the receiver uses the parts. **mixed** is several different things packed together (body plus attachments), and the receiver wants all of them. **alternative** is several versions of the same content, and the receiver's program picks the one it can display best, not all of them:
text.zh: multipart 有几种，区别在收信方怎么用这些段。**mixed** 是几份不同的东西装在一起（正文加附件），收信方全都要。**alternative** 是同一份内容的几种版本，收信方的程序挑一种它显示得最好的，不是都显示：

blocks.code:
Content-Type: multipart/alternative; boundary=B2 --B2 Content-Type: text/plain Hi Bob, see you at 3. --B2 Content-Type: text/html

Hi Bob, see you at 3.

--B2--

caption.en: multipart/alternative: two versions of the same sentence, only one is shown
caption.zh: multipart/alternative：同一句话的两个版本，只显示一个

title.en: mixed or alternative?

prompt.en: Alice is sending two messages. Message A: a paragraph of explanation, plus a PDF report and a photo. Message B: the same greeting, which her program attaches in both a plain-text version and an HTML version. Which multipart should each message's Content-Type use?
prompt.zh: Alice 要发两封信。甲：一段说明文字，外加一份 PDF 报告和一张照片。乙：同一段祝福，她的程序同时附上纯文本版和 HTML 版。两封信的 Content-Type 各该用哪种 multipart？

label.en: A uses mixed, B uses alternative
label.zh: 甲用 mixed，乙用 alternative

feedback.en: Right. The receiver wants all three things in A; the two versions in B say the same sentence, so showing one is enough.
feedback.zh: 对。甲的三样东西收信方都要；乙的两个版本说的是同一句话，挑一个显示就行。

label.en: Both use mixed
label.zh: 两封都用 mixed

feedback.en: The plain text and the HTML in B are the same greeting; with mixed, the receiver would show it twice.
feedback.zh: 乙里的纯文本和 HTML 是同一句祝福，用 mixed，收信方就会把它显示两遍。

label.en: A uses alternative, B uses mixed
label.zh: 甲用 alternative，乙用 mixed

feedback.en: That is backwards. With alternative in A, the receiver's program would display only one of the parts, and the PDF or the photo would not be seen.
feedback.zh: 反了。甲用 alternative，收信方的程序只会挑其中一份显示，PDF 或照片就看不到了。

label.en: Both use alternative
label.zh: 两封都用 alternative

feedback.en: B is right, A is not: A's text, PDF and photo are three different things, so you cannot pick just one.
feedback.zh: 乙对，甲不对：甲的文字、PDF、照片是三份不同的东西，不能只挑一份。

explain.en: One question tells them apart: are these parts “all wanted” or “pick one”? All wanted is mixed; pick one is alternative. As for how the receiver knows where one part ends and the next begins, that is the boundary line.
explain.zh: 问一个问题就能分清：这几段是“都要”还是“挑一个”？都要用 mixed，挑一个用 alternative。至于收信方怎么知道一段到哪里结束、下一段从哪里开始，靠的是 boundary 那一行。

title.en: The SMTP dialogue: walking through it line by line

text.en: An SMTP dialogue is all ASCII text, question and answer: the client sends a **command**, and the server replies with a **response code** and a sentence. Alice's server (client C) connects to port 25 of Bob's server (S), sets up a TCP connection, and then:
text.zh: SMTP 的对话全是 ASCII 文本，一问一答：客户端发**命令**，服务器回**响应码**加一句话。Alice 的服务器（客户端 C）连上 Bob 的服务器（S）的 25 端口，建好 TCP 连接，然后：

blocks.code:
S: 220 mail.ee.uwa.edu.au SMTP service ready
C: HELO mail.unimelb.edu.au
S: 250 mail.ee.uwa.edu.au says hello
C: MAIL FROM:<alice@student.unimelb.edu.au>
S: 250 sender ok
C: RCPT TO:<bob@ee.uwa.edu.au>
S: 250 recipient ok
C: DATA
S: 354 Send mail; end with a single dot on a line by itself
C: From: alice@student.unimelb.edu.au
C: To: bob@ee.uwa.edu.au
C: Subject: hello
C:
C: Hi Bob, ...
C: .
S: 250 message accepted
C: QUIT
S: 221 mail.ee.uwa.edu.au closing connection

caption.en: One SMTP dialogue (adapted from the slides)
caption.zh: 一次 SMTP 对话（改自课件）

rows.en: 220: the server says I am ready. HELO: the client introduces itself. 250: fine, hello.
rows.zh: 220：服务器说我准备好了。HELO：客户端报上自己。250：好，你好。

rows.en: MAIL FROM and RCPT TO are the envelope, each getting a 250. After DATA, 354 means please begin sending, followed by the header and body, and a lone dot on a line by itself shows the message is finished, to which the server replies 250 to show it has accepted the message.
rows.zh: MAIL FROM 和 RCPT TO 是信封，各得到一个 250。DATA 之后 354 的意思是请开始发，随后是首部和正文，最后单独一行的点表示信发完了，服务器回 250 表示信已收下。

rows.en: QUIT asks to end, and 221 is the server saying goodbye.
rows.zh: QUIT 要求结束，221 是服务器道别。

text.en: If Bob's server is temporarily unreachable, Alice's server does not throw the message away, but puts it in a queue and tries again after a while. This is the work behind what we said earlier, “the sender can leave as soon as the message is handed over”.
text.zh: 如果 Bob 的服务器暂时连不上，Alice 的服务器不会把信扔掉，而是放进队列，隔一阵再试。这就是前面说的“发信人交出去就能走”背后的功夫。

text.en: The submission step (port 587) speaks the same language, the difference being that it usually requires authentication first: Alice's server sends mail on behalf of its own users, and without verifying identity anyone could use it to send spam. Port 25 is for receiving between servers: the other side is also a mail server, which has to accept mail addressed to its own users anyway, so no authentication is required.
text.zh: 提交那一步（587 端口）说的是同一种话，区别在于通常要先认证：Alice 的服务器是替自己的用户发信，不核实身份，谁都能借它发垃圾邮件。25 端口是服务器之间收信：对面也是一台邮件服务器，本来就要接收发给自己用户的信，所以不要求认证。

text.en: The strengths and weaknesses can also be seen from here: it is all plain ASCII, so people can read it directly, and it is easy to debug and implement; but every small step has to wait for the other side to reply before continuing, so one message takes many round trips.
text.zh: 优缺点也从这里看得出来：全是明文 ASCII，人能直接读、好调试、好实现；但每个小步骤都要等对方回一句才能继续，一封信要来回很多次。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: the first digit of the response code
summary.zh: 超出课件：响应码的第一位

text.en: The first digit of an SMTP response code follows a pattern: 2 means success, 3 means please continue, 4 means a temporary error, try again later (queue retries rely on this), and 5 means a permanent error.
text.zh: SMTP 响应码的第一位有规律：2 表示成功，3 表示请继续，4 表示暂时出错、稍后再试（队列重试就靠它），5 表示永久出错。

title.en: Strengths and weaknesses of SMTP

prompt.en: A classmate looked at an SMTP dialogue and said: “It is all plain-text and question-and-answer, which is far too primitive; it should be binary and send everything in one go.” Name one strength and one weakness of SMTP's current design, and give your reasons.
prompt.zh: 一位同学看了 SMTP 的对话说：“全是明文文字、一问一答，太原始了，应该改成二进制、一次把所有东西发完。”请说出 SMTP 现在这种设计的一个优点和一个缺点，并说明理由。

key_points.en: Strength: a simple text protocol that is easy to read, debug and implement
key_points.zh: 优点：简单的文本协议，容易读、调试和实现

key_points.en: Weakness: one message needs many round trips
key_points.zh: 缺点：一封信需要多次来回交互

key_points.en: Gives reasons by referring to what the dialogue looks like
key_points.zh: 能结合对话的样子说明理由

model_answer.en: Strength: it is a simple ASCII text protocol, so commands and responses can be read directly, and it is easy to implement and debug. Weakness: every step has to wait for the other side's response, so sending one message takes many round trips, which is inefficient (and binary content also has to be encoded first).
model_answer.zh: 优点：它是简单的 ASCII 文本协议，命令和响应都能直接读，容易实现和调试。缺点：每个步骤都要等对方回应，发一封信要来回很多次，效率不高（另外二进制内容还得先编码）。

explain.en: The strength comes from “everything is text people can read”, and the weakness comes from “question and answer”. Simplicity in the design is paid for with more round trips.
explain.zh: 优点来自“全是人能读的文字”，缺点来自“一问一答”。设计上的简单换来了交互次数的增加。

title.en: Final delivery: POP3 and IMAP

text.en: In the last step, Bob fetches his mail from his own server, and there are two protocols for it. The difference comes down to one sentence: **where the mail stays**.
text.zh: 最后一步，Bob 去自己的服务器取信，有两个协议。它们的区别就在一句话：**信留在哪里**。

rows.en: Downloaded to the device the user agent runs on, and no longer kept on the server
rows.zh: 下载到用户代理所在的这台设备，服务器上不再保留

rows.en: Stays on the server, and the device only goes to look
rows.zh: 留在服务器上，设备只是去看

rows.en: Once the phone has downloaded it, the laptop cannot see it
rows.zh: 手机下载了，笔记本就看不到

rows.en: All devices see the same mailbox, with read status and folders consistent
rows.zh: 各设备看到同一个邮箱，已读、文件夹都一致

rows.en: Simple: connect and pull the mail down
A set of commands that manage the mailbox on the server directly
rows.zh: 一套命令直接管理服务器上的邮箱

text.en: The IMAP server runs on port 143 of the receiving server, and the user agent is its client. LOGIN logs in, LIST lists folders, CREATE makes a new one, COPY copies a message into it, DELETE removes one: these commands all work on the mailbox on the server, so on another device you see the very same thing.
text.zh: IMAP 的服务器跑在收信服务器的 143 端口，用户代理是它的客户端。LOGIN 登录，LIST 列出文件夹，CREATE 新建一个，COPY 把信拷进去，DELETE 删掉：这些命令都是在服务器上的邮箱里动手，所以换一台设备，看到的还是同一份。

text.en: So POP3 suits the era of a single device, and IMAP was designed for multiple devices.
text.zh: 所以 POP3 适合只有一台设备的年代，IMAP 是为多设备设计的。

title.en: Phone and laptop

prompt.en: On your phone you read a message and dragged it into the “Homework” folder, and you want to see exactly the same state when you open your laptop. Which protocol should you use to fetch mail?
prompt.zh: 你在手机上把一封信读了、拖进了“作业”文件夹，希望打开笔记本时看到一模一样的状态。该用哪个协议取信？

feedback.en: POP3 downloads the mail to one device and no longer keeps it on the server. The laptop cannot see how you organised things on the phone.
feedback.zh: POP3 把信下载到一台设备，服务器上不再保留。笔记本看不到手机上的整理结果。

feedback.en: Right. The mail and the folders are on the server, so every device sees the same mailbox.
feedback.zh: 对。信和文件夹都在服务器上，各设备看到的是同一个邮箱。

feedback.en: SMTP pushes mail out (submission and the transfer between servers); it does not fetch mail.
feedback.zh: SMTP 是把信推出去（提交和服务器之间传输），不是取信。

explain.en: What you want is “one mailbox, viewed from many places”, which is only possible if the mail stays on the server.
explain.zh: 要的是“同一份邮箱，多处查看”，这只有信留在服务器上才做得到。

title.en: Webmail: the browser as the user agent
title.zh: 网页邮件：浏览器当用户代理

text.en: The user agent so far was a program installed on your computer, such as Outlook. **Webmail** (such as Gmail) does it differently: the user agent is a set of web pages in the browser. You write and read messages on web pages, while the mail work behind them is still done by servers. Which protocol is used for which leg, see the diagram:
text.zh: 前面的用户代理是装在电脑上的程序，比如 Outlook。**网页邮件** (webmail，如 Gmail) 换了个做法：用户代理是浏览器里的一组网页。你在网页上写信、读信，背后的邮件工作仍由服务器做。哪一段用哪个协议，看图：

alt.en: Webmail: HTTP between the browser and the web front end; SMTP from the web front end to the mail server for submission; SMTP between the two mail servers; to read mail, the web front end fetches it from the mailbox using a custom interface or IMAP or POP3
alt.zh: 网页邮件：浏览器与网页前端之间用 HTTP；网页前端提交给邮件服务器用 SMTP；两家邮件服务器之间用 SMTP；取信时网页前端从邮箱取信，用自定义接口或 IMAP、POP3

caption.en: The protocol used for each leg in webmail
caption.zh: 网页邮件里，每一段用的协议

items.en: **Submission**: the browser hands the message to the web front end over HTTP, and the front end then hands it to the mail server over SMTP.
items.zh: **提交**：浏览器用 HTTP 把信交给网页前端，前端再用 SMTP 交给邮件服务器。

items.en: **Transfer**: between servers it is still SMTP, exactly as when using Outlook.
items.zh: **传输**：服务器之间仍然是 SMTP，和用 Outlook 时一模一样。

items.en: **Fetching**: the web front end takes the message out of the mailbox (inside the server, using a custom interface, or IMAP or POP3), and then sends the page to the browser over HTTP.
items.zh: **取信**：网页前端从邮箱里把信取出来（服务器内部，用自定义接口，或者 IMAP、POP3），再用 HTTP 把页面送到浏览器。

text.en: So the browser end speaks only HTTP. HTTP is just that short stretch between the user agent and the server; how mail travels between servers has not changed at all.
text.zh: 所以浏览器这一头只说 HTTP。HTTP 只是用户代理和服务器之间的那一小段，邮件在服务器之间怎么走，一点没变。

title.en: Which leg is HTTP?

prompt.en: Alice writes a message with webmail in her browser, to Bob, who is at another company and reads his mail with a desktop program. Along the whole path, which leg uses HTTP?
prompt.zh: Alice 在浏览器里用网页邮件写信，发给在另一家公司、用桌面程序收信的 Bob。整条路里，哪一段用的是 HTTP？

label.en: Only the leg from Alice's browser to her webmail server
label.zh: 只有 Alice 的浏览器到她的网页邮件服务器这一段

feedback.en: Right. The browser is Alice's user agent, and it speaks HTTP to the server; everything after that is mail's own protocols.
feedback.zh: 对。浏览器是 Alice 的用户代理，它和服务器之间说 HTTP；往后都是邮件自己的协议。

label.en: Between the two companies' mail servers
label.zh: 两家公司的邮件服务器之间

feedback.en: Transfer between servers is still SMTP; webmail does not change that step.
feedback.zh: 服务器之间的传输仍然是 SMTP，网页邮件没有改变这一步。

label.en: From Bob's desktop program to Bob's server
label.zh: Bob 的桌面程序到 Bob 的服务器这一段

feedback.en: Bob uses a desktop user agent, which fetches mail over POP3 or IMAP. Only if Bob also used webmail would his end be HTTP.
feedback.zh: Bob 用的是桌面用户代理，取信走 POP3 或 IMAP。要是 Bob 也用网页邮件，他那一头才是 HTTP。

label.en: The whole path is HTTP, because Alice uses a browser
label.zh: 整条路都是 HTTP，因为 Alice 用的是浏览器

feedback.en: The browser is only the shell of the user agent. Moving the message between servers still relies on SMTP.
feedback.zh: 浏览器只是用户代理的外壳。信在服务器之间搬运，靠的还是 SMTP。

explain.en: HTTP appears only between the browser and the web front end. Server to server is always SMTP; Bob uses a desktop program, so he fetches mail over POP3 or IMAP.
explain.zh: HTTP 只出现在浏览器和网页前端之间。服务器到服务器永远是 SMTP；Bob 用桌面程序，取信走 POP3 或 IMAP。

title.en: How long to wait if you download everything first?
title.zh: 先下载完再播要等多久

prompt.en: A movie is 1 GB (about 8000 Mbit), and your connection is a steady 20 Mbit/s. The simplest approach is to download the whole movie before playing. How many seconds do you wait before it starts?
prompt.zh: 一部电影 1 GB（约 8000 Mbit），你的网速稳定在 20 Mbit/s。最简单的办法是整部下载完再播。开播前要等多少秒？

explain.en: 8000 ÷ 20 = 400 seconds, nearly 7 minutes. Is there a way to play while downloading? That is what streaming media sets out to solve.
explain.zh: 8000 ÷ 20 = 400 秒，接近 7 分钟。有没有办法边下边播？这就是流媒体要解决的事。

title.en: Streaming media: pickier than ordinary data
title.zh: 流媒体：比普通数据更挑剔

text.en: Streaming media comes in three kinds:
text.zh: 流媒体 (streaming media) 分三类：

rows.en: The content has long been on the server
Live broadcast of a sports event
The content is produced on the spot and viewers join at any time
rows.zh: 内容现场产生，观众随时接入

rows.en: The two sides talk in real time; most sensitive to delay
rows.zh: 双方实时对话，延迟最敏感

text.en: Compared with web pages and email, it is pickier in two ways: it needs much more **bandwidth**; and it is much more sensitive to **delay** and **jitter**. Jitter means packets arriving at uneven times: a packet should come every 20 milliseconds, but sometimes two arrive 5 milliseconds apart, and sometimes one arrives only after 60 milliseconds. A web page arriving 1 second late does not matter, while a video arriving a little late freezes for a moment.
text.zh: 和网页、邮件相比，它挑剔两点：要的**带宽**高得多；对**延迟**和**抖动** (jitter) 敏感得多。抖动指包到达的时间忽快忽慢：本来每 20 毫秒应该来一个包，结果有时隔 5 毫秒来两个，有时隔 60 毫秒才来一个。网页晚 1 秒到无所谓，视频晚一点就卡一下。

text.en: The “download everything, then play” approach just mentioned is the slides' simplest method: the browser uses HTTP to save the whole file to disk and then hands it to the player. The benefit is no real-time problems; the cost is that the user waits idly.
text.zh: 刚才那个“全部下完再播”，就是课件里的最简单做法：浏览器用 HTTP 把整个文件存到硬盘，再交给播放器。好处是没有实时问题，代价是用户要干等。

title.en: Dedicated models: metafile, RTSP and RTP
title.zh: 专用模型：元文件、RTSP 和 RTP

text.en: The slides' simplest approach downloads the whole file over HTTP and then hands it to the player: you have to wait for the whole file to arrive, and in the meantime you cannot tell the server “play from minute 10” or “pause”. Dedicated schemes split the work up.
text.zh: 课件里的最简单做法，是用 HTTP 把整个文件下载下来，再交给播放器：要等文件整个到齐，期间也没法对服务器说“从第 10 分钟播”或者“暂停”。专用方案把活分开了。

text.en: A browser only speaks HTTP and cannot understand a media stream. So what the web server gives it is just a small “pick-up slip” called a **metafile**, which says where the media is. The browser glances at the file type and hands it to a dedicated **media player**; the player then follows the slip to the **media server** to ask for the stream.
text.zh: 浏览器只会 HTTP，也看不懂媒体流。所以网页服务器交给它的只是一张小小的“取货单”，叫**元文件** (metafile)，上面写着媒体在哪。浏览器看一眼文件类型，就把它交给专门的**媒体播放器**；播放器再按单子去找**媒体服务器**要流。

alt.en: The browser gets the metafile from the web server over HTTP and hands it to the media player; the player then sends control commands to the media server over RTSP, and the media server sends data back over RTP
alt.zh: 浏览器通过 HTTP 向网页服务器取元文件，交给媒体播放器，播放器再用 RTSP 向媒体服务器发控制命令，媒体服务器用 RTP 回传数据

caption.en: Get the metafile, hand over, control, send data
caption.zh: 取元文件，交接，控制，传数据

text.en: Once the stream is flowing, three things each handle their own part:
text.zh: 拿到流以后，三样东西各管一摊：

rows.en: Commands such as play, pause and record (PLAY, PAUSE, RECORD), like a remote control
rows.zh: 播放、暂停、录制 (PLAY、PAUSE、RECORD) 等命令，像遥控器

rows.en: Delivers the media packet by packet: it does not retransmit by itself, supports multicast, and each packet carries a timestamp (telling the player at what moment to play it). It usually runs over UDP; the slides' figure says “TCP or UDP”, so it can also be carried over TCP
rows.zh: 把媒体一个个包送过来：自己不重传，支持多播，每个包带时间戳（告诉播放器它该在什么时刻播）。通常跑在 UDP 上，课件图里写的是“TCP 或 UDP”，也可以放在 TCP 上

rows.en: How the content is squeezed smaller before being sent; the compression step later explains it in detail
rows.zh: 内容怎么压小再传，后面压缩那一步细讲

text.en: There is a reason control and data travel separately: the remote control's commands are few and not one may be lost; the media data is plentiful, and meeting the deadline matters more than losing none.
text.zh: 控制和数据分开走是有道理的：遥控器的命令很少，一条都不能丢；媒体数据很多，赶时间比一个不丢更重要。

text.en: Why does RTP dare not to retransmit? We answer that when we discuss packet loss. The variant carried over TCP will be used again when we discuss live streaming.
text.zh: RTP 为什么敢不重传？讲丢包时回答。放在 TCP 上的那种用法，讲直播时还会用到。

title.en: Whose job is the pause button?

prompt.en: You are watching a lecture recording in a media player, and it is already playing. You press pause. Over which protocol, and to whom, is this “pause” command sent?
prompt.zh: 你用媒体播放器看一段讲座录像，已经在播了。你按下暂停键。这条“暂停”命令是用什么协议、发给谁的？

label.en: RTSP, to the media server
label.zh: RTSP，发给媒体服务器

feedback.en: Right. RTSP handles control, and PLAY and PAUSE are its commands; the media server is the one sending the stream.
feedback.zh: 对。RTSP 管控制，PLAY、PAUSE 都是它的命令；媒体服务器才是发流的一方。

label.en: RTP, to the media server
label.zh: RTP，发给媒体服务器

feedback.en: RTP delivers the media data packet by packet; it is not a remote control.
feedback.zh: RTP 管的是把媒体数据一个个包送过来，它不是遥控器。

label.en: HTTP, to the web server
label.zh: HTTP，发给网页服务器

feedback.en: The web server's job was finished when it handed over the metafile; after that the player deals directly with the media server.
feedback.zh: 网页服务器的活在元文件交出去时就做完了，之后播放器直接和媒体服务器打交道。

label.en: MPEG-4, to the player
label.zh: MPEG-4，发给播放器

feedback.en: MPEG-4 is a compression format that decides how the content is squeezed smaller; it is not a protocol for sending commands.
feedback.zh: MPEG-4 是压缩格式，管内容怎样压小，不是传命令的协议。

explain.en: The three things have different jobs: RTSP controls, RTP carries data, MPEG-4 compresses. Pausing is control, so it is RTSP; data packets still travel by RTP, except that the server stops sending once it receives the command.
explain.zh: 三样东西分工不同：RTSP 控制，RTP 传数据，MPEG-4 压缩。暂停是控制，所以是 RTSP；数据包照样走 RTP，只是服务器收到命令后不再发了。

title.en: Jitter and buffering: store up a little before playing
title.zh: 抖动与缓冲：先攒一点再播

text.en: Jitter comes from changes in bandwidth (such as network congestion, Lesson 13) and from retransmission after packet loss. The countermeasure is plain and effective: the client first stores arriving data in a **buffer**, and the player plays from the buffer. The network speeds up and slows down, but with stock in the buffer, playback does not stall.
text.zh: 抖动的来源是带宽的变化（比如网络拥塞，第 13 课），以及丢包后的重传。对策朴素而有效：客户端先把到的数据攒进**缓冲区**，播放器从缓冲里取着播。网络忽快忽慢，缓冲里有存货，就不卡。

text.en: Buffer size is a trade-off. Suppose the video is 2 Mbit per second and the network averages 4 Mbit/s. If the buffer stores up only 1 second (2 Mbit), playback can start in 0.5 seconds, but a brief network stall will empty it. If it stores up 10 seconds (20 Mbit), you wait 5 seconds before playback starts, but a stall of a few seconds in the middle does not matter. A small buffer starts fast and resists jitter weakly; a large buffer makes you wait more but is steady.
text.zh: 缓冲大小是一个权衡。设视频每秒 2 Mbit，网络平均 4 Mbit/s。缓冲只攒 1 秒（2 Mbit），0.5 秒就能开播，但网络停一下就见底。攒 10 秒（20 Mbit）要等 5 秒才开播，但中间停个几秒也无所谓。小缓冲开播快、抗抖动弱；大缓冲要多等、但稳。

alt.zh: 媒体服务器的数据经缓冲区送往播放器，缓冲区内有低水位线和高水位线，灰色表示已攒的数据

caption.en: The buffer and its two water marks

text.en: Two **water marks** let the buffer regulate itself. Take some numbers: suppose the high-water mark is 10 seconds of stock and the low-water mark is 4 seconds.
text.zh: 两条**水位线**让缓冲区自己调节。举个数：设高水位线是存货 10 秒，低水位线是 4 秒。

items.en: After playback starts, the stock keeps rising until it reaches 10 seconds (the **high-water mark**): the player tells the server to pause for now, so it does not keep pouring data in, saving bandwidth and memory.
items.zh: 开播后存货一路涨，涨到 10 秒（**高水位线** high-water mark）：播放器通知服务器先暂停，不必一直猛灌，省带宽，也省内存。

items.en: With the server stopped, the player is still eating stock one second at a time, and it falls to 4 seconds (the **low-water mark**): the player tells the server to resume sending.
items.zh: 服务器停了，播放器还在一秒一秒地吃存货，一路降到 4 秒（**低水位线** low-water mark）：播放器通知服务器恢复发送。

items.en: The “please resume” message takes a round trip to reach the server and for new data to come back, and in that time the player is still eating stock. The low-water mark is not set at 0 precisely to leave this safety margin, so that the supply is topped up before the bottom is reached.
items.zh: “请恢复”这句话传到服务器、新数据再传回来，要一个来回的时间，这期间播放器还在吃存货。低水位线不设在 0，就是留着这点安全余量，赶在见底之前补上货。

items.en: So the stock swings between 4 and 10 seconds: it never runs dry, and never bursts.
items.zh: 于是存货在 4 到 10 秒之间摆动：既不见底，也不撑爆。

title.en: How big should the buffer be?

prompt.en: The video is 2 Mbit per second. You want playback not to stall even if the network stops for up to 4 seconds. How many Mbit of stock must the buffer hold at least?
prompt.zh: 视频每秒 2 Mbit。你想让播放在网络最多停 4 秒的情况下也不卡。缓冲区里至少要有多少 Mbit 的存货？

hints.en: In those 4 seconds when the network stops, the player consumes 2 Mbit every second.
hints.zh: 网络停的这 4 秒里，播放器每秒都要消耗 2 Mbit。

explain.en: 4 seconds × 2 Mbit/s = 8 Mbit. The stock in the buffer must last through the longest stall; but the more stock there is, the longer you wait before playback starts.
explain.zh: 4 秒 × 2 Mbit/s = 8 Mbit。缓冲里的存货要能撑过最长的那次停顿；但存货越多，开播前要等的越久。

title.en: Packet loss: why not retransmit, and what to do
title.zh: 丢包：为什么不重传，怎么办

text.en: RTP runs over UDP: what is lost is lost, with no retransmission. This is not laziness. Think of a call: the player is about to play packet 5 in 20 milliseconds, and it is lost. To retransmit, you must first notice, then ask, then wait for the resend, which takes a round trip of at least (say) 80 milliseconds. By the time the packet arrives, its playback moment is long past and it is useless. Worse, TCP-style retransmission would make the packets behind it queue up waiting for it as well (Lesson 12).
text.zh: RTP 跑在 UDP 上，丢了就丢了，不重传。这不是偷懒。想想一段通话：播放器在 20 毫秒后就要播第 5 个包，它丢了。要重传，得先发现、再请求、再等重发，一个来回至少就是（假设）80 毫秒。包来了，它的播放时刻早过了，已经没用。更糟的是，TCP 式的重传会让后面的包也排队等它（第 12 课）。

text.en: So the playback software has to find its own way around packet loss, with three tricks:
text.zh: 所以丢包要播放软件自己想办法，有三招：

rows.en: Send some extra redundancy, and recompute what was lost from the redundancy
rows.zh: 多发一些冗余，丢了就用冗余算回来

rows.en: Put a recovery marker in the compressed data at close intervals, so after a loss decoding can pick up again from the next marker rather than ruin everything after it
rows.zh: 在压缩数据里每隔很近就放一个恢复标记，丢包后解压能从下一个标记接着来，不至于后面全毁

rows.en: Guess a plausible replacement to patch the gap, for example estimating the lost frame by interpolating between the frames before and after it
rows.zh: 猜一个像样的来补，如用前后两帧插值估出丢的那一帧

text.en: Retransmission makes little sense for interactive conferencing such as video calls, for the same reason: it arrives too late.
text.zh: 重传对视频通话这类交互式会议没什么意义，原因同上：来得太晚。

alt.en: Four data packets A, B, C, D plus a parity packet P; B is lost on the way, and the receiver recovers B by XORing P, A, C and D bit by bit
alt.zh: 四个数据包 A、B、C、D 加一个校验包 P，B 在路上丢了，接收方用 P、A、C、D 逐位异或算回 B

caption.en: FEC: one parity packet for every 4 data packets
caption.zh: FEC：每 4 个数据包配 1 个校验包

text.en: The ⊕ in the figure is bitwise exclusive-or. Next we work it through with concrete bits.
text.zh: 图里的 ⊕ 是按位异或。接下来用具体的比特算一遍。

title.en: FEC: recovering one packet with one parity packet
title.zh: FEC：用一个校验包救回一个包

intro.en: For every 4 data packets, add 1 parity packet P, which is the bitwise XOR of those 4 packets. The rule for exclusive-or (XOR, written ⊕): two equal bits give 0, two different bits give 1. It has a handy property: XORing the same number twice leaves it unchanged. Let us choose four 4-bit packets ourselves: A = 1011, B = 0110, C = 1100, D = 0101. (XOR will turn up again later in cryptography.)
intro.zh: 每 4 个数据包再加 1 个校验包 P，P 是那 4 个包按位异或的结果。异或 (XOR，记作 ⊕) 的规则：两位相同得 0，不同得 1。它有个好用的性质：同一个数异或两次，等于没动。我们自己选 4 个 4 位的包：A = 1011，B = 0110，C = 1100，D = 0101。（异或在后面的密码学里还会再见到。）

why.en: Compare bit by bit: write 0 when equal, 1 when different
why.zh: 逐位比较，相同写 0，不同写 1

why.en: Finally XOR in D to get the parity packet. P is unlike any of the four data packets; it is a “fingerprint” kneading all four together. The sender sends A, B, C, D and P all together
why.zh: 最后异或 D，得到校验包。P 和四个数据包都不一样，它是把四个包揉在一起的“指纹”。发送方把 A、B、C、D、P 一起发出去

why.en: The receiver has A, C, D and P

lines.tex: P\oplus A\oplus C\oplus D = B\oplus(A\oplus A)\oplus(C\oplus C)\oplus(D\oplus D) = B

why.en: P originally contains A, B, C and D; XOR A, C and D out once more each and they cancel each other (X ⊕ X = 0), leaving only B
why.zh: P 里本来含着 A、B、C、D；再把 A、C、D 各异或一次，它们各自抵消（X ⊕ X = 0），只剩 B

why.en: Now plug in the numbers and XOR them one by one
why.zh: 现在代入数字，一项项异或

why.en: Finally XOR in D, which gives exactly the lost B
why.zh: 最后异或 D，正是丢掉的 B

outro.en: Cost and limit: one parity packet is one equation and can solve only one unknown, so if two packets in the same group are lost, they cannot be recovered. The cost is 1 extra packet for every 4 data packets, so the redundancy overhead is 1/4. The smaller the groups, the stronger the protection and the higher the overhead: with 1 parity packet for every 2 packets, the overhead is 1/2. The slides also mention that Hamming codes and Reed-Solomon codes can do the same kind of job (Hamming codes are in Lesson 6).
outro.zh: 代价和限制：一个校验包只有一个方程，只能解出一个未知数，所以同一组里丢两个包就救不回来。代价是每 4 个数据包多发 1 个，冗余开销是 1/4。组分得越小，保护越强，开销越大：每 2 个包配 1 个校验包，开销就是 1/2。课件还提到汉明码和里德-所罗门码 (Reed-Solomon) 也能做同类的事（汉明码见第 6 课）。

title.en: What was lost is C

prompt.en: Same group, but this time C is lost. The receiver has A = 1011, B = 0110, D = 0101, P = 0100. What is the recovered C?
prompt.zh: 还是这一组，但这次丢的是 C。接收方有 A = 1011，B = 0110，D = 0101，P = 0100。还原出的 C 是什么？

feedback.en: Right. C = P ⊕ A ⊕ B ⊕ D.
feedback.zh: 对。C = P ⊕ A ⊕ B ⊕ D。

feedback.en: 1000 is A ⊕ B ⊕ D; it forgot to XOR in the parity packet P.
feedback.zh: 1000 是 A ⊕ B ⊕ D，忘了把校验包 P 异或进去。

feedback.en: 0100 is P itself. P is the XOR of the four packets, not C.
feedback.zh: 0100 就是 P 本身。P 是四个包的异或，不是 C。

label.en: It cannot be recovered, because the parity packet only protects the last packet D
label.zh: 无法还原，因为校验包只能保护最后一个包 D

feedback.en: The parity packet treats all four packets alike and can solve for whichever is lost. The limit is on the number: only one may be lost in the same group.
feedback.zh: 校验包对四个包一视同仁，丢哪一个都能解。限制在数量：同一组里只能丢一个。

explain.en: P ⊕ A = 1111, ⊕ B gives 1001, ⊕ D gives 1100. Any one packet can be lost, as long as only one is lost in the group. If B and C were both lost, there would be only one equation and two unknowns, and they could not be recovered.
explain.zh: P ⊕ A = 1111，再 ⊕ B 得 1001，再 ⊕ D 得 1100。丢任何一个包都行，只要这一组只丢一个。要是 B 和 C 同时丢了，手里只有一个方程、两个未知数，就救不回来。

title.en: Compression: encoding can be slow, decoding must be fast
title.zh: 压缩：编码可以慢，解码要快

text.en: Multimedia files are large. Compression saves bandwidth and transfer time: the sender **encodes** and the receiver **decodes**. The two algorithms are asymmetric: encoding can be slow and resource-hungry (the producer does it once), while decoding must be fast and must not need expensive hardware (every viewer's phone has to do it). The slides' example: 200 kB compressed to 20 kB for transmission, then restored to 200 kB on arrival, so the transfer is only one tenth of the original.
text.zh: 多媒体文件很大。压缩能省带宽、省传输时间：发送方**编码**，接收方**解码**。这两个算法是不对称的：编码可以慢、耗资源（制作方一次性做完），解码必须快，也不能要昂贵硬件（每个观众的手机都得做）。课件的例子：200 kB 压成 20 kB 传过去，到了再还原回 200 kB，传输量只有原来的十分之一。

text.en: Is the restored version exactly like the original? There are two kinds:
text.zh: 还原回来是不是和原来一模一样？分两类：

rows.en: Restored exactly, not one bit different
The structure of the data itself: repetition and patterns
rows.zh: 数据本身的结构：有重复、有规律

rows.en: The limits of human perception (perceptual encoding)
rows.zh: 人的感知局限（感知编码, perceptual encoding）

rows.en: Bills, programs, documents: one wrong bit is an error
rows.zh: 账单、程序、文档：错一位就是错

rows.en: Sound, images, video: differences people cannot notice do not matter
rows.zh: 声音、图像、视频：人察觉不到的差别无所谓

text.en: Look at lossless first, which relies on structure: repeated content is written only once. The smallest example: record aaaaaaaaaabbb as 10a3b, and 13 characters become 5, and unpacking gives back exactly the same text. The methods zip and PNG use are far more refined, but the idea is the same: find the repetition and patterns in the data and use a shorter way to write them.
text.zh: 先看无损，它靠的是结构：重复的内容只写一次。最小的例子：把 aaaaaaaaaabbb 记成 10a3b，13 个字符变成 5 个，解开后一字不差。zip 和 PNG 用的办法比这精巧得多，思路相同：找出数据里的重复和规律，换一种更短的写法。

text.en: What does lossy throw away? Take sound: the human ear has different sensitivity at different frequencies. The curve in the figure below is called the hearing threshold: at a given frequency, a sound must be louder than the curve to be heard. Sound below the curve cannot be heard at all, and keeping it only wastes space. MP3 throws this part away.
text.zh: 有损丢掉的是什么？以声音为例，人耳对不同频率的灵敏度不同。下图的曲线叫听阈：在某个频率上，声音必须比曲线响才听得到。曲线以下的声音，根本听不到，留着也白占空间。MP3 就把这部分丢掉。

alt.zh: 听阈曲线：横轴是频率，纵轴是声音强度，曲线以下的区域是人耳听不见的，可以丢掉

caption.en: Sound below the curve is inaudible, and lossy compression can drop it
caption.zh: 曲线以下的声音听不见，有损压缩可以丢掉它

text.en: Images work the same way: JPEG keeps a little less of the detail the eye is not sensitive to. Put the numbers out and you can see whether it is worth it (these figures are common values, not given in the slides): one stretch of CD-quality stereo is 44100 × 16 × 2 = 1411200 bit per second, about 1.4 Mbit/s; stored as a 128 kbit/s MP3 it is about 11 times smaller, and for everyday music listening most people cannot hear an obvious difference. Lossless audio compression commonly reaches about half the original size. Accepting a little loss that people cannot perceive in exchange for a much larger compression ratio is why multimedia almost always uses lossy compression.
text.zh: 图像同理：JPEG 少留一点眼睛不敏感的细节。把数字摆出来，就知道值不值（这几个数是常见值，课件没给）：一段 CD 音质的立体声，每秒 44100 × 16 × 2 = 1411200 bit，约 1.4 Mbit/s；存成 128 kbit/s 的 MP3，小了约 11 倍，日常听音乐多数人听不出明显差别。无损压缩音频，常见的是压到原来的一半左右。接受一点人感觉不到的损失，换来大得多的压缩比，这就是多媒体几乎都用有损的原因。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: video has one more layer, and audio has masking
summary.zh: 超出课件：视频多出一层，音频还有掩蔽效应

text.en: In video, two adjacent frames are often much alike. An encoder like H.264 first exploits this structure: it records only what changed in this frame compared with the last. Like lossless compression, this relies on the structure of the data and not on human perception; only afterwards does it use perceptual limits to throw away detail that cannot be seen. Stacking the two layers is what makes video so small.
text.zh: 视频的画面在相邻两帧之间往往大同小异。H.264 这样的编码器先利用这种结构：只记这一帧比上一帧变了哪里。这和无损压缩一样，靠的是数据本身的结构，不是人的感知；之后再用感知局限丢掉看不出的细节。两层叠起来，视频才压得这么小。

text.en: For audio, next to a very loud sound, quieter sounds are also covered up and cannot be heard (the masking effect), and encoders drop those too. The slides go only as far as the hearing threshold curve.
text.zh: 音频方面，一个很响的声音旁边，较轻的声音也会被盖住听不见（掩蔽效应），编码器也会一起丢掉。课件只讲到听阈曲线。

title.en: Which is lossless and which is lossy?

prompt.en: You want to compress two things before sending them: the electronic text of a bank statement, and a holiday photo. Which one must use lossless compression, and which suits lossy compression? Then say in your own words: what is lossy compression, and why does almost all multimedia rely on it?
prompt.zh: 你要把两样东西压小再发出去：一份银行对账单的电子文本，和一张度假照片。哪个必须用无损压缩，哪个适合有损压缩？再用你自己的话说：什么是有损压缩，为什么多媒体几乎都靠它？

key_points.en: The statement must be lossless: one wrong digit changes the meaning, so it must be restored exactly
key_points.zh: 对账单必须无损：错一位数字意思就变了，需要精确还原

key_points.en: Lossy compression: the decoded data is only an approximation of the data before encoding, not identical
key_points.zh: 有损压缩：解码出来的数据只是编码前数据的近似，并不完全相同

key_points.en: Multimedia often uses perceptual-encoding-based lossy compression, dropping what people cannot see or hear
key_points.zh: 多媒体常用基于感知编码的有损压缩，丢掉人看不到、听不到的部分

key_points.en: Accepting a small loss of information in exchange for a large compression ratio, saving bandwidth and transfer time
key_points.zh: 接受少量信息损失，换来很大的压缩比，省带宽和传输时间

model_answer.en: The bank statement must be lossless: one wrong digit changes the whole meaning, so it has to be restored exactly, compressed by exploiting repetition and patterns in the data. The photo suits lossy compression. Lossy compression means the decoded data is only an approximation of the original data and cannot be restored exactly. Multimedia often uses lossy compression based on perceptual encoding, which drops the parts the eye cannot see and the ear cannot hear; only a little information is lost, yet a very high compression ratio is obtained, saving a great deal of bandwidth and transfer time.
model_answer.zh: 银行对账单必须无损：错一位数字，意思就全变了，所以要能精确还原，靠数据里的重复和规律来压。照片适合有损。有损压缩是指解码得到的数据只是原始数据的近似，不能完全还原。多媒体常用基于感知编码的有损压缩，丢掉人眼看不出、耳朵听不到的部分，只损失一点点信息，却能得到很高的压缩比，省下大量带宽和传输时间。

explain.en: Which to choose depends on “whether anyone cares about what is thrown away”: in a statement one wrong bit is an error, while in a photo nobody cares about detail the eye cannot see. Multimedia accepts this small loss in exchange for a much larger compression ratio.
explain.zh: 选哪种，看“丢掉的东西有没有人在乎”：账单里错一位就是错，照片里丢掉人眼看不出的细节没人在乎。多媒体接受这点损失，换来大得多的压缩比。

title.en: Live streaming: how one stream reaches a hundred thousand people
title.zh: 直播：一份流怎样给十万人

text.en: **Live**: the content is produced on the spot and viewers join at any time. As with on-demand viewing, the client uses a buffer to smooth out jitter. The difficulty is at the other end: 100,000 people watch one live stream at the same time, each stream at 2 Mbit/s. If a single server sent a separate stream to each viewer, the total output would be 100000 × 2 Mbit/s = 200 Gbit/s, which one server simply cannot bear.
text.zh: **直播** (live)：内容现场产生，观众随时接入。和点播一样，客户端用缓冲抹平抖动。难处在另一头：一场直播有 10 万人同时看，每路流 2 Mbit/s。如果一台服务器给每个观众单独发一路，出口总共是 100000 × 2 Mbit/s = 200 Gbit/s，一台服务器根本扛不住。

text.en: The ideal approach is **IP multicast** plus RTP over UDP: the sender sends only one copy, routers copy it along the way as needed, and each viewer receives one. The difference between the two approaches:

caption.en: Multicast versus one stream per person

text.en: But the slides say that in practice TCP is used. The reason is that IP multicast may work only inside an operator's own network and fail across networks. With multicast unusable, there is no choice but to **send a separate stream to each viewer**, which brings us back to 200 Gbit/s.
text.zh: 可课件说，实际用的是 TCP。原因是 IP 多播可能只在运营商自己的网络里才能用，跨网络就不通。多播用不了，就只好**给每个观众单独发一路流**，这就回到了 200 Gbit/s。

text.en: When one server cannot cope, a group of servers share the load, called a **content delivery network** (CDN). The servers are spread around the world, and each serves only the nearby batch of viewers. Suppose each has 10 Gbit/s of output, so 100,000 people need 20 servers; the live source only has to send the stream to each of the 20 once, and they distribute the rest.
text.zh: 一台服务器扛不住，就用一组服务器分担，叫**内容分发网络** (CDN)。这组服务器分布在各地，每台只服务附近的一批观众。假设每台出口 10 Gbit/s，10 万人要 20 台；直播源头只需把流送给这 20 台各一份，剩下的由它们分发。

title.en: Beyond the slides: why TCP for the one-to-one leg
title.zh: 超出课件：为什么一对一的这一路用 TCP

body.en: The slides say only “TCP is used in practice” without elaborating. The usual reason is that once multicast does not work, each viewer and the server have an ordinary one-to-one connection, TCP is ready-made, it retransmits lost data automatically, so there is no need to find another way yourself; and a live stream already keeps a few seconds of buffer, so there is enough time for retransmission.
body.zh: 课件只说“实际用 TCP”，没有展开。常见的理由是：多播不通以后，每个观众和服务器之间就是一条普通的一对一连接，TCP 是现成的，丢了自动重传，用不着自己再想办法；而直播本来就留着几秒缓冲，重传的时间够用。

text.en: Does this contradict the earlier statement that “RTP runs over UDP and does not retransmit”? No, it depends on whether you can afford to wait. A live stream has a few seconds of buffer and can afford to wait, so TCP retransmission is fine; a call cannot afford to wait, so it uses UDP, and what is lost is lost. (RTP itself does not retransmit; when it is carried over TCP, the retransmission is done by TCP.) Next, calls.
text.zh: 这和前面说的“RTP 跑在 UDP 上、不重传”矛盾吗？不矛盾，要看等不等得起。直播有几秒缓冲，等得起，所以 TCP 重传没问题；通话等不起，所以用 UDP，丢了就丢了。（RTP 本身不重传；放在 TCP 上时，重传是 TCP 做的。）接下来看通话。

title.en: Voice and video conferencing: late means lost
title.zh: 语音和视频会议：来晚就等于丢了

text.en: **Voice and video conferencing** (VoIP, voice over IP) is the pickiest about delay. Two people talk back and forth, and when a sentence arrives a few hundred milliseconds late, they talk over each other or fall silent. A live stream is willing to wait a few extra seconds for stability, but a call cannot spare a single millisecond, so every approach is the opposite of live streaming:
text.zh: **语音和视频会议** (VoIP，voice over IP) 对延迟最挑剔。两个人你一句我一句，一句话晚到几百毫秒，就会抢话、冷场。直播愿意多等几秒换稳，通话一毫秒都舍不得，所以每条做法都和直播反着来：

rows.en: Every millisecond in the buffer is a millisecond both sides wait longer. A few seconds stored up in a live stream is harmless, but a few seconds in a call makes conversation impossible.
rows.zh: 缓冲里的每一毫秒，都是双方多等的一毫秒。直播攒几秒无所谓，通话攒几秒就没法聊。

rows.en: Skip packets that arrive too late
That sentence has already passed, and nobody will listen to a replay; waiting for it would also slow the packets behind. Lose a packet or two and paper over it with error concealment.
rows.zh: 那句话已经过去了，补播也没人听；等它还会拖慢后面的包。丢一两个包，用差错掩盖糊过去。

rows.en: When the network is poor, lower the picture quality and frame rate, so there is less data and packets can arrive in time; better a bit blurry than frozen.
rows.zh: 网络差时降画质、降帧率，数据少了，包才来得及；宁可糊一点，也别卡住。

rows.en: Reserve resources for the stream, or mark packets with Differentiated Services so routers forward them first. The details are not in this lesson; it is enough to know the method exists.
rows.zh: 给流预留资源，或给包打上差分服务 (Differentiated Services) 标记，让路由器优先转发。细节不在这一课，知道有这个办法就行。

text.en: There is one more problem we have not touched so far: Alice wants to call Bob, knowing only his name, not which device he is on right now, nor which encodings his device can decode. This step is handled by the application-layer protocol **Session Initiation Protocol** (SIP): it finds the callee, establishes the capabilities on both sides, and then sets up, manages and ends the session, whether two-party, multi-party or multicast. A call goes like this:
text.zh: 还有一个问题前面都没碰：Alice 想打给 Bob，只知道他的名字，不知道他此刻在哪台设备上，也不知道他的设备能解哪几种编码。这一步由应用层协议**会话发起协议** (Session Initiation Protocol, SIP) 负责：找到被叫、确定双方的能力，然后建立、管理、结束会话，两方、多方或多播的都行。一次通话是这样走的：

alt.zh: 一次通话的时间线：SIP 先找到 Bob 并协商编码，Bob 接听后双方用 RTP 传声音和画面，最后用 SIP 挂断

caption.en: SIP connects and hangs up; RTP carries sound and picture
caption.zh: SIP 牵线和收线，RTP 搬声音和画面

text.en: The division of labour is clear: SIP only connects and disconnects the call, and the sound and picture themselves travel over RTP. It is like the telephone exchange that connects the line, while the talking is up to you.
text.zh: 分工很清楚：SIP 只管牵线和收线，声音和画面本身走的是 RTP。就像电话局负责接通线路，说话是你们自己的事。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: what a SIP message looks like
summary.zh: 超出课件：SIP 的消息长什么样

text.en: The invitation in step ① is called INVITE; Bob's device first replies 180 Ringing, replies 200 OK once he answers, and Alice replies ACK to confirm, and only then does the call begin; step ④ is called BYE. SIP messages, like SMTP and HTTP, are text. The slides only require you to know what things SIP does.
text.zh: 第①步的邀请叫 INVITE，Bob 的设备先回 180 Ringing（响铃），接听后回 200 OK，Alice 再回 ACK 确认，通话才开始；第④步叫 BYE。SIP 的消息和 SMTP、HTTP 一样是文本。课件只要求知道 SIP 做哪几件事。

title.en: The road this lesson has travelled

body.en: A single click in your browser may trigger, besides a web page, email and video. Email relies on two always-online servers passing the baton; video relies on buffering, redundancy and compression to cope with an unreliable network.
body.zh: 你的浏览器一次点击，除了网页，还可能触发邮件和视频。邮件靠两台常年在线的服务器接力，视频靠缓冲、冗余和压缩，对付一个不可靠的网络。

title.en: A call on a congested network

prompt.en: You are writing an international video call app. The network suddenly becomes congested, packets arrive at uneven times, and a few are lost. Which approach is the most suitable?
prompt.zh: 你在写一个跨国视频通话软件。网络突然拥塞，包到达得忽快忽慢，还丢了几个。下面哪种做法最合适？

label.en: Enlarge the buffer to several seconds and wait for the packets to arrive before playing
label.zh: 把缓冲加大到好几秒，等包到齐再播

feedback.en: This is the approach for watching a live stream: a big buffer is steady, but every sentence is heard seconds late, and two people cannot hold a conversation.
feedback.zh: 这是看直播的办法：缓冲大，稳，但每句话都晚几秒才听到，两个人没法对话。

label.en: Retransmit every lost packet, so none are missing
label.zh: 让每个丢掉的包重传，一个都不少

feedback.en: A retransmitted packet arrives long after its playback moment and is useless; it also makes the packets behind queue up for it, making the delay worse.
feedback.zh: 重传来的包早过了播放时刻，没用；还会让后面的包排队等它，延迟更糟。

label.en: Skip packets that arrive too late, and lower the video quality when the network is poor so there is less data
label.zh: 来得太晚的包直接跳过，网络差时降低视频质量，让数据变少

feedback.en: Right. In a call a late packet is as good as lost, so skip it; lowering quality makes the data smaller so packets are more likely to arrive on time.
feedback.zh: 对。通话里晚到的包等于丢了，宁可跳过；降质量让数据少些，包更容易准时到。

label.en: Switch to IP multicast, so routers do the copying for you
label.zh: 改用 IP 多播，让路由器替你复制

feedback.en: Multicast solves the sender's burden in one-to-many delivery, not delay and loss. A call is one-to-one, so it does not apply.
feedback.zh: 多播解决的是一对多时发送方的负担，不是延迟和丢包。通话是一对一，用不上。

explain.en: A call needs low delay. Keep the buffer small, skip late packets and, if necessary, lower the picture quality: these go together as one approach, better to lose a little than to let the conversation slow down. SIP had already found the other party and negotiated the encoding before the call; once the call begins, these methods govern how the sound and picture flow.
explain.zh: 通话要的是低延迟。缓冲要小，晚到的包跳过，必要时降画质，这几条是一套：宁可丢一点，也不能让对话变慢。SIP 在通话之前已经把对方找到、把编码谈好了；通话开始之后，这些办法管的是声音和画面怎样流动。
